messages.subject: Number of points in marginal
parts:
Hi! Is it possible to adjust the points at which the marginals are calculated?

By default it seems to calculate at 31 points, but this does not capture the shape at the mode of the distribution very well (compared to distribution from MCMC) and interpolating doesn't really help. Can I ask inla for more points or spread them out differently?

Joe

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Number of points in marginal
parts:
On Thu, 2016-02-25 at 06:32 -0800, Joe S wrote:
> Hi! Is it possible to adjust the points at which the marginals are
> calculated?
>
> By default it seems to calculate at 31 points, but this does not
> capture the shape at the mode of the distribution very well (compared
> to distribution from MCMC) and interpolating doesn't really help. Can
> I ask inla for more points or spread them out differently?

to follow up on this. the most recent testing version using more points
(unless the model is HUGE). if you're looking at hyperparameters, and
want to transform them, then its usually much safer, to start from the
marginals in `the internal scale', which is log(precision), say, and
transform from those. 

like here

> r = inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y = rnorm(10)))
> m1 = inla.tmarginal(function(prec) 1/sqrt(prec),
r$marginals.hyperpar[[1]])
> m2 = inla.tmarginal(function(logprec) 1/sqrt(exp(logprec)),
r$internal.marginals.hyperpar[[1]])


'm2' would be the most accurate one, in general.
